iyor.title: -iyor · Happening Now
lines: "-iyor" works like English "-ing". Dans ediyorum = I am dancing 💃
Verb stem + iyor + person: gel → geliyorum (I'm coming) · git → gidiyor (she's going — t softens to d!)
Negative: slip in -m- : içmiyorum = I am NOT drinking 🚭

mi.title: mi? · The Floating Question
lines: Turkish makes questions with a tiny floating word: mi / mı / mu / mü ❓
It vowel-harmonizes with the word before it: Güzel mi? (Is it beautiful?) · Türk müsün?
Kokteyl var mı? = Is there a cocktail? (asking for a friend 🍹)

poss.title: Possessives · -im / -in
lines: benim ...-im = my · senin ...-in = your
benim köpeğim = my dog 🐶 (k softens to ğ!)
senin bisikletin = your bike 🚲 · Add -le for "with": köpeğimle = with my dog

ecek.title: -ecek / -acak · The Future
lines: Stem + -ecek (after e i ö ü) or -acak (after a ı o u), then the person ending.
geleceğim = I will come 🚶‍♀️ · yapacağım = I will do · yağmur yağacak = it will rain 🌧
The k softens to ğ before a vowel — that is why it is geleceğim, not "gelecekim".
Negative slips -mi/-mı in front: gelmeyeceğim = I will not come 🙅‍♀️

di.title: -di · The Past You Saw
lines: For things you witnessed yourself. Stem + -di / -dı / -du / -dü (or -ti/-tı/-tu/-tü after a hard consonant).
gittim = I went 🚶‍♀️ · gördüm = I saw 👀 · okudu = she read 📖
Compare with -miş, which is for things you only heard about. gelmiş = apparently he came 🤷‍♀️
Hüseyin's thirty years of stories are all in -di, because he was there for every one.

meli.title: -meli / -malı · Must and Should
lines: Stem + -meli (e i ö ü) or -malı (a ı o u) = ought to, should, must.
gitmeliyim = I must go · çay içmelisin = you should drink tea 🍵
Birisi bir şey yapmalı = somebody should do something — the teyze's favourite sentence.
For a softer "have to" Turkish also uses lazım: gitmem lazım = I need to go.

se.title: -se / -sa · If
lines: Stem + -se / -sa sets up a condition. Yağmur yağarsa = if it rains 🌧
Vaktim olsa yürürdüm = if I had time, I would walk 🐕
Paired with -ardı/-erdi it becomes the "would have" of things that never happened.
Keşke + -se is the great Turkish sigh: keşke gelsen = if only you would come 💭

plural.title: Plurals · -ler / -lar
lines: e-type harmony: e i ö ü → -ler · a ı o u → -lar
evler = houses 🏠 · arabalar = cars 🚗
BUT after numbers, no plural! iki köpek = two dogs (never "iki köpekler") 🔢

vowel.title: Vowel Harmony · The Deep Magic
lines: Every suffix listens to the LAST vowel of the word. This is the engine of all Turkish 🎛️
i-type suffixes have 4 forms (ı/i/u/ü): plajda, evde, Antalya'dan
-de/-da = at · -e/-a = to · -den/-dan = from. Rawr. 🦖

loc.title: At the Café · -de/-da + Ordering
lines: -de / -da = at, in: kafede = at the café ☕ · plajda = at the beach
Ordering: Bir çay lütfen = one tea please · Hesap lütfen = the bill please 🧾
When food arrives, they say: Afiyet olsun! = enjoy your meal 😋

NPCS.name: DISKOTEK KING 👑

task.desc: Defeat 8 monsters — keep the dance floor safe

reward.msg: 👑 +100₺ — "The floor is safe. Sen bir kraliçesin." (You are a queen.)

greet: Merhaba dansçı kız! 💃 (Hello dancer girl!) I am the Diskotek King.
My club speaks only Turkish after midnight. Let me teach you the -iyor tense — the tense of RIGHT NOW, of the dance floor!
chat: Gece daha yeni başlıyor! (The night is just beginning!)

NPCS.name: DJ COOL CAT 🐱

task.desc: Bring 3 cocktails for the booth (don't drink them all)

greet: Miyav. 🐱 I am DJ Cool Cat. I ask the important questions...
And in Turkish, questions FLOAT. Let me teach you the magic little word mi.
chat: Müzik mi? Aşk mı? İkisi de. 🎧 (Music or love? Both.)

NPCS.name: BANDIT'S FRIEND 🦴

task.desc: His bone washed up on the beach — find it! 🏖️

reward.msg: 🦴 Bandit Strike cooldown 25s → 18s! The dogs are allies now.

greet: Hav hav! 🐶 (Woof woof — but you knew that.)
Bandit's best friend here. Dogs understand possession deeply: MY bone. Let me teach you -im/-in... then find my bone. Lütfen.
chat: Hav! Kemiğim nerede? 🦴 (Where is my bone?)

NPCS.name: LITTLE BLONDE COUSINS 👧👦

task.desc: They want 5 seashells for their collection 🐚

greet: Torii abla! Torii abla! 👋 (Big sis Torii!)
We know Turkish numbers AND plurals! Wanna learn? It's -ler or -lar, the vowels DECIDE, it's SO cool—

NPCS.name: DİNOZOR EFENDİ 🦖

task.desc: Defeat 10 monsters — the Capitol lawn must stay peaceful

reward.msg: 🦖 +1 INT — "65 million years of vowel harmony wisdom. Rawr."

greet: *adjusts fez* Merhaba. Evet, I am a dinosaur in Turkish clothes. 🦖🧿
I have watched this language evolve for 65 million years. Sit, child. Vowel harmony is the deep magic.
chat: Rawr demek "merhaba" demek. Bazı dillerde. (Rawr means hello. In some languages.)

NPCS.name: FIVE SIPS OWNER ☕

task.desc: The café is out of simit — bring 4 from Trader Joe's district

reward.msg: ☕ +50₺ & SHOP OPEN! Talk to him anytime to buy supplies.

greet: Hoş geldin kızım. ☕ (Welcome, my girl.) Five sips — that's all a proper Turkish coffee needs.
Sit. Before you buy anything, learn to ORDER like a local. The suffix -de/-da...

NPCS.name: BAHÇIVAN NURİ 🌱

task.desc: Three öküz have been trampling the gardens — see them off

reward.msg: 🌱 +260₺ — "Bahçem kurtuldu! My garden is saved. Sen bir meleksin."

greet: Kolay gelsin! 🌱 (May it come easy — what you say to someone working.)
Öküzler bahçemi çiğniyor. The oxen are trampling my garden. If you deal with them, I will teach you how Turkish talks about the future — because I am planning next spring already.
chat: Yağmur yağacak. (It is going to rain.)

NPCS.name: DEFNE (7) 🪁

task.desc: Defne lost her kite — bring her 2 bright things to trade

greet: Abla! Abla! 🪁 (Big sister! — what a kid calls any older girl.)
Uçurtmam ağaca takıldı. My kite is stuck in the tree. Do you have anything shiny to trade? I know a question trick I can teach you — the little word mi!

NPCS.name: BAKKAL HÜSEYİN 🥖

task.desc: Clear 10 monsters off the Yeşiltepe streets

reward.msg: 🥖 +300₺ and beads. "Afiyet olsun. Mahalle sana borçlu." (The neighbourhood owes you.)

greet: Hoş geldin komşu! 🥖 (Welcome, neighbour!) I have run this shop for thirty years.
Thirty years means a lot of stories, and stories need the past tense. Clear my street and I will teach you -di.

NPCS.name: MERAKLI TEYZE 👀

task.desc: Teyze insists it is not safe — prove it by clearing 6 monsters

reward.msg: 👀 +200₺ — "Ben demiştim! I said so! But you were brave, kızım." 🍪

greet: Kızım, sen kimin kızısın? 👀 (Girl, whose daughter are you? — the classic teyze opener.)
This neighbourhood has gone downhill. Somebody should do something about it. Funnily enough that is exactly the grammar I can teach you: -meli, must and should.
chat: Perdeden bakıyorum. (I am watching from behind the curtain.)

NPCS.name: KÖPEKÇİ SELİM 🐕

task.desc: Walk the hill with him — clear 12 monsters along the way

reward.msg: 🐕 +280₺ — his dog and Bandit have become inseparable. arkadaş = friend.

greet: Ooo, senin köpeğin de var! 🐕 (Oh, you have a dog too!) Bandit, değil mi?
I walk these hills every evening. If I had more time I would walk them all day — and that "would" is the grammar I can give you: -se.
chat: Yürüyüş yapıyoruz. (We are going for a walk.)

SOUL.d: the çay auntie — refills your glass before it is empty
hi: Gel gel, otur kızım! Çayın hazır. ☕
Merhaba demeyi bilmeyen adam olmaz. Unit 1 benden.

SOUL.d: Torii's best friend — knows every one of her secrets
hi: TORİİİİ! 😭 Seni özledim!
Okay okay okay — introductions, numbers, "I am / you are". Unit 2. Sit.

SOUL.d: perpetually stressed, speaks in latte foam metaphors
hi: Order up! Uh — I mean — buyurun! ☕
Ordering, commands, directions. Unit 3. I do this 400 times a day.

SOUL.d: still a dog. just upright today. nobody at the café discusses it.
hi: Hav— ahem. Merhaba. 🐶
*sits back down on his haunches, then remembers, and stands again*
MY bone. MY ball. MY human. Possession, Unit 4. I am an expert in this.

SOUL.d: her fiancé, playing the same four chords forever
hi: Bebeğim! Otur, sana bir şey çalayım. ❤
The past tense, and telling the time. Unit 5. Where we started.

SOUL.d: Torii's brother — makes beats, ignores deadlines
hi: Yo sis. Listen to this one. 🎧
The future tense and making suggestions. Unit 6. "Let's" is my whole personality.

SOUL.d: long hair, long beard, one bicycle, infinite stories
hi: HEYYY! Bisikletimi gördün mü? 🚲
Requests, wanting things, and TELLING STORIES. Unit 7. Oh I have stories.

SOUL.d: enormous. fluffy. from the old neighbourhood. a legend.
hi: *mrrrrrp* 🐈
Comparisons. Unit 8. I am bigger than every other cat. This is a fact, not an opinion.

SOUL.d: chain-smoking, moustachioed, furious, patriotic about a country he has never visited
hi: *lights a Camel Soft off the previous Camel Soft*
"Sigara içen insan, sağlıklı insandır." (A person who smokes is a healthy person.) This is science.
Obligation, likes, dislikes, and GIVING ADVICE. Unit 9. I have advice about everything.

SOUL.d: they speak in the plural. they are one guy.
hi: "Trick me, trick me, gods of Trickery." Say it back. Go on.
Conditionals. IF. MAYBE. PERHAPS. Unit 10. Nothing is certain, least of all us.

SOUL.d: Josh's cat. she has seen things in that garage.
hi: *stares at a spot slightly above your head*
Complaints, apologies, and REPORTED SPEECH. Unit 11. I know what everyone said about you.

SOUL.d: knows every street. has opinions about all of them.
hi: Nereye abla? 🚕
"The street THAT..." "The guy WHO..." Relative clauses. Unit 12. My whole job is describing places.

SOUL.d: blonde, small, extremely loud, know everything about everyone
hi: TORİİ ABLA! TORİİ ABLA!
Duyduk ki— (We heard that—) the -miş tense! Unit 13! Everything we know is a rumour!

SOUL.d: yes, that one. he summers in Antalya. he is from here, actually.
hi: Ho ho— merhaba kızım! 🎅
"Back in my day..." The past habitual. Unit 14. I have a LOT of days to draw from.

SOUL.d: linguist. will explain a suffix until the sun goes down.
hi: Ah! A learner! Sit, sit. 📚
The passive voice and word-building suffixes. Unit 15. My favourite unit. My FAVOURITE.

SOUL.d: a green budgie on a brass perch. has listened to this family for sixteen years.
hi: *a small green budgie hops sideways along a brass bar and tilts his head at you*
Bana "Kuşum" derler. (They call me Kuşum — "my little bird".) Herkes böyle der. 🐦
On altı yıl bu evde oturdum. Herkesi dinledim. (Sixteen years in this house. I listened to everyone.)
Ve en çok duyduğum kelime "keşke" oldu. (And the word I heard most was "keşke" — if only.)
Pişmanlık ve olmayan geçmiş. Unit 16. Son ünite, canım. (Regret and the past that never happened. The final unit.)
